transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a request from our corporate counterparty to increase their approved derivatives exposure limit from $20 million to $35 million. Before I make a decision, I'd like to follow our usual process. Let's start with credit risk -- could you walk us through the counterparty's current credit profile and your assessment of this requested increase?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we proceed. I received the counterparty's updated rating assessment this morning. Under the bank's single-name limit matrix, the counterparty's current rating band permits a maximum derivatives exposure limit of exactly $28,000,000. This assessment has not yet been entered in the committee pack, so you may not have seen it. Based on this, the requested increase to $35 million would exceed the maximum permitted under the rating band, though an increase up to $28 million would be within the allowable limit.
